bib.title: Convolutional Neural Networks for Sentence Classification

question: Can a simple one-layer CNN over pre-trained word vectors classify sentences well, and does fine-tuning or freezing the vectors matter?
hypothesis: Pre-trained word vectors are universal feature extractors that help across tasks; a two-channel (static plus fine-tuned) model was hoped to reduce overfitting.
contributions: Simple CNN with static word2vec vectors and little tuning is strong on 7 benchmarks
Multichannel variant combining static and fine-tuned vectors
Improves state of the art on 4 of 7 tasks

method.summary: A single convolution layer with filter widths 3, 4, 5 over concatenated word vectors, max-over-time pooling, dropout and a softmax layer. Four variants: random init, static word2vec, fine-tuned word2vec, and two-channel.
method.task: sentence classification (sentiment, subjectivity, question type, opinion polarity)

models.name: CNN-static
models.architecture: same, word2vec frozen (unknown words random, also frozen)

models.name: CNN-multichannel
models.architecture: two channels both init from word2vec; gradients only through one

training.optimizer: SGD over shuffled mini-batches with Adadelta update rule
training.epochs: early stopping on dev set; number not stated
training.regularisation: l2-norm constraint s=3 on weight vectors
training.seeds: inferred: CV-fold assignment, unknown-word init and CNN init kept fixed within each dataset; number of runs not stated

other.filters: windows h=3,4,5 with 100 feature maps each
other.tuning: grid search on SST-2 dev set; 10% of train held out as dev when no standard dev set
other.sst_note: SST-1/2 trained on phrases and sentences, scored on sentences only
other.unknown_word_init: random; slight gain from U[-a,a] matching pre-trained variance

other.test_time: weights scaled by p, no dropout

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: test set accuracy (10-fold CV mean where no standard split)

eval.protocol: Single reported number per cell; no variance or significance test stated.

evidence.quote: filter windows (h) of 3, 4, 5 with 100 feature maps each, dropout rate (p) of 0.5, l2 constraint (s) of 3, and

results.claim: Fine-tuning moves 'good' away from 'bad': in word2vec good is most similar to bad, which is no longer so after fine-tuning on SST-2.

results.claim: Pre-trained vectors are described as universal feature extractors reusable across tasks.

limits: Multichannel gains over single channel are mixed; authors say further work on regularising fine-tuning is warranted
No variance, seeds count or significance tests reported
Hyperparameters tuned on SST-2 dev only, then reused
Unclear whether word2vec beats Collobert's Wikipedia vectors because of architecture or the 100B-word corpus
Static word vectors are context-free; superseded by contextual models

terms.definition: static: word vectors kept fixed during training; non-static: fine-tuned by backpropagation
two sets of word vectors, each filter applied to both, gradients through only one
take the max of each feature map as that filter's feature, handling variable sentence length
